ruleset.name: Opinionated Rules
ruleset.description:
Opt-in checks that are deliberately NOT part of the default `go` ruleset because they conflict with idiomatic Go. They come straight from PHPMD's object-oriented, PHP-flavoured heritage, and flag patterns that are perfectly normal — often unavoidable — in Go.
You can run these if you want a stricter, more opinionated style, but they are not part of "idiomatic Go":
* CleanCode/ElseExpression flags every `else` branch. Go uses `else` freely; early returns are encouraged but not required, and `gofmt`/`go vet`/golint do not object to `else`. * CleanCode/BooleanArgumentFlag flags every boolean parameter. Go's own standard library is full of them (e.g. strconv, io, signal), so this is an OO Single-Responsibility opinion rather than a Go convention. * UnusedCode/UnusedFormalParameter flags unread parameters. In Go, parameters are routinely kept to satisfy an interface, an http.HandlerFunc signature, sort.Interface, or a callback shape — the compiler deliberately allows unused parameters for exactly this reason. * Design/GlobalVariable flags mutable package-level variables. Global mutable state hurts testability and concurrency safety, but some package-level variables are idiomatic in Go (sentinel errors, compiled regexps, registries), so this is left out of the default `go` ruleset.
Run with: messgo <paths> <format> opinionated Or combine: messgo <paths> <format> go,opinionated

rule.name: UncheckedTypeAssertion
rule.message: The {0} {1}() uses an unchecked type assertion that panics on failure. Use the comma-ok form (v, ok := x.(T)) or a type switch.
rule.description:
A Go-specific rule (no PHPMD analog). Flags type assertions used without the comma-ok form (v, ok := x.(T)), which panic on a failed assertion. The comma-ok form and type switches (switch v := x.(type)) are safe and not flagged.
This rule is opinionated because unchecked assertions are sometimes intentional (the caller knows the type is correct), but they are a common source of panics in production.

rule.name: IdenticalBranches
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has identical branches. Combine or extract to avoid copy-pasted logic.
rule.description:
A Go-specific rule (no PHPMD analog). Flags if/else and switch cases whose bodies are textually identical, which usually indicates copy-pasted logic that belongs in a single path. Two branches are "identical" when their statements produce the same formatted output.
This rule is opinionated because identical branches can be legitimate (e.g. default cases that must return the same value), but they are usually a sign of missing abstraction.

rule.name: StructEmbeddingDepth
rule.message: The {0} {1} has an embedding depth of {2}. The configured embedding depth threshold is {3}. Deep embedding chains obscure promoted fields and methods.
rule.description:
A Go-specific rule (no PHPMD analog, but the conceptual cousin of PHPMD's DepthOfInheritance). Flags structs whose transitive embedding chain exceeds a threshold (default 3). Deep embedding chains make it hard to understand which promoted fields and methods a type exposes.
Cross-package embeddings are approximate: the AST alone cannot resolve them, so they are treated as depth-0 leaves. Within-package embeddings are followed transitively across files.
This rule is opinionated because embedding is idiomatic in Go, but chains deeper than 3-4 levels are rarely intentional and usually indicate a type hierarchy disguised as embedding.
